#2687. Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season

EUGENE — One of Oregon football's most important defensive players is done for the season.

Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon's 41-28 win over Ohio State, Dan Lanning announced on Monday.

"Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he's been here," Lanning said. "Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum's done for the year, he had a knee injury, he'll end up having surgery."

Tuioti was among the Ducks' leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front.

In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game.

"I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on," Lanning said. "He left it on the line there on the field, and I don't know if he'll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky."

Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts.

#2682. Warriors' surprising turnaround has changed everything about their present - and future

The Golden State Warriors are heading out on their first extended road trip of the season and they're packing a few items that no one would have expected just two weeks ago. An 8-3 record. And a slot in the top four in the Western Conference.

Yeah, it's early. Very early. The season is only 13% complete. There are many ups and downs, stories and challenges ahead. But after an 0-3 start that seemed to confirm the worst of the skeptics' scenarios, the Warriors have transformed into a team that has not only been fun to watch but is creating bright scenarios for the future.

"We're doing all the things we need to convince ourselves we're the team we think we can be," Stephen Curry said recently.

What is the cause of this dramatic change in fortunes and vibe?

Is it the magic in the building, left over from the Valkyries' spectacular playoff run?

Possibly, and I'm not even kidding. Synergy between teams and coworkers is a real thing. Winning teams raise the bar for all the other franchises in their market: sibling teams definitely push each other even more. The Warriors were totally invested in the Valkyries' success, showing up at games, repping their gear, celebrating with them. And the Valkyries reminded the veteran Warriors of all the joy that comes with winning together.

Is it my provocative question to Curry on Warriors media day, when I asked him how it felt that some people don't expect them to even make the playoffs and he said "Damn!" and walked off the podium?

I am kidding about that moment, specifically. But, in general, the Warriors are a very proud group and they were well aware of the lowered expectations surrounding a team that was once only spoken of in terms of championship runs. Starting 0-3 made that negative noise louder.

"It's hard not to hear it," Curry said. "We try not to play into it. We hate losing."

Is the turnaround the result of something that initially looked demoralizing but could end up being a blessing in disguise? The unavailability of Kristaps Porzingis?

Porzingis never even got his season started, has since stepped away from basketball and the Warriors stopped paying his salary. The development has meant that Steve Kerr has gone with a lineup that allows rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to play power forward instead of small forward, a better fit, and also to play Draymond Green at center where he continues to play well. Not waiting around for the theoretical return of Porzingis also means the Warriors know exactly where they stand when February's trade deadline rolls around.

Or is this bounce in the Warriors' play due to just one factor? The new guy?

"Yax," Curry has said, more than once, when asked what's different. Lendeborg, the 11th pick in last June's draft, has been a revelation and has become an instant and integral part of the Bay Area sports landscape. His immediate impact has changed so many negative narratives around the Warriors, such as Kerr doesn't like rookies or general manager Mike Dunleavy doesn't know what he's doing.

"Our second best player is a rookie," Green said Saturday night. "He's only played 10 games."

The Warriors will face heightened competition on this long trip: They start with the Rockets and Spurs, currently two of the top five teams in the West, and also a revenge match against Memphis, which beat the Warriors in their home opener. When they come home Nov. 22, they host the Celtics, one of the top teams in the East.

The Warriors are still just getting started but there's a lot to like right now. The team feels like it's on a different trajectory. Curry is playing at superstar level, averaging 30.6 points a game, and (knock wood) doesn't seem to be hampered by his knee issues. The depth of the team allows Kerr to limit veteran minutes. Lendeborg is making non-Steph minutes survivable.

"My take is we're a very resilient team," Curry said.

The team entered Tuesday ranked second in offensive rating and 11th in defensive rating. On Monday Kerr said, "We have a chance to be, I think, a top-10 offense and defense. And that's what it takes to be a great team in this league, a real contender. And that's our goal."

Also important: the Warriors look like they're having fun again. They seem connected, energized and the chemistry is good. Jimmy Butler's amusing turn as an assistant coach on Monday, sitting on the bench in coaching gear, carrying a clipboard with the instruction "PASS TO STEPH" is one example.

The hope is for Butler to be back in about two months. The Warriors hope to be in a position to make a move at the trade deadline in early February. All of a sudden, not only does the Warriors' future look promising, the present is surprisingly bright.

#2681. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2678. Las Vegas Raiders get their gold mined by the 49ers

The Las Vegas Raiders traveled to Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California, to renew the Battle of the Bay rivalry with the San Francisco 49ers. A rivalry that has meant so much to the two fan bases. Turnovers were the story of this contest. When the clock read zero, the Raiders had committed five turnovers and allowed 30+ points on defense for the sixth straight week.

Kirk Cousins had his worst game as the signal caller for the Raiders. In the first half, he only threw the ball eight times. By the end, Cousins threw three interceptions, with one pick-six after recovering his own fumble. Things simply did not go his way today.

Ashton Jeanty regained his starting position and managed 25 yards on six carries. In the passing game where he has made his largest impact, he caught five passes for -5.0 yards. Mike Washington Jr. was subjected to simply awful run blocking, finishing the game with -3.0 yards on six carries with a long of four yards.

Bowers played his first game near his hometown of Napa, California, with reportedly around 50 friends and family in attendance. He would punish the 49ers, finishing with 111 yards on seven catches, including a 21-yard score. A questionable spot robbed him of a second touchdown.

Early on, Raiders defensive playcaller Rob Leonard continued getting his lunch money stolen by an opposing offensive play caller. The 49ers drove down the field on the opening possession in 12 plays, five passes, seven runs and scored. On the second possession, the 49ers ran the ball down the Raiders' throats. Brock Purdy, the 49ers quarterback, would finish the game with 40 yards rushing on seven carries. Including a rushing touchdown which put the 49ers up 14-0.

By the end of the 49ers third drive the Raiders defense surrendered 94 yards rushing, while being on the field for every play except three with 1:52 seconds to play in the first quarter. What we heard from the television broadcasters was that it was 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan's goal to run the ball 40 times against the Raiders' putrid run defense.

After going three-and-out on their first drive, Kirk Cousins gets settled in and hits passes to Jack Bech, Brock Bowers, and Jalen Nailor. Driving the Raiders downfield when the end of the quarter makes them switch sides. Cousins finishes the drive off with his team leading with the second rushing touchdown of the year. Drawing the Raiders to within a score.

Raiders' defense continued to allow nearly six yards per carry to the 49ers offense. On 4th and 1, the run blocking of the 49ers knocked the Raiders' defenders three yards off the line of scrimmage. Raiders followed it up by running some type of zone blitz where both defensive tackles dropped into zone coverage and surrendered a passing touchdown to McCaffrey.

After a Raiders offensive possession netting a field goal, the Raiders were down 21-10 and needed a defensive stop to close out the half. Maxx Crosby would get his fourth sack of the season and a false start penalty would end the half. At the end of the half, the 49ers had ran the ball 25 times for 125 yards and two touchdowns.

First play of the second half, Cousins fumbled the football, picked it up and threw a pick-6, 17 seconds into the second half. Exactly what the Raiders could not afford to have happen. To be fair, everything is resting on his shoulders and in order for the Raiders to have any chance of winning any game, he can't afford to make a mistake.

In the retribution drive after the turnover, Cousins came right back, completing seven of seven throws. finishing with a 21-yard touchdown pass to Bowers to level the score at 28-17. Mistakes happen, but atoning for them is critical. With just under 10 minutes remaining in the 3rd quarter, the 49ers offense would take the field for the first time in the second half.

Treydan Stukes, the Raiders' second-round pick, fooled Purdy, intercepted the pass, tried to fall numerous times with no one around to tackle him and stumbled back to the 30-yard line of the 49ers. Momentum shifts are a huge thing, giving the Raiders an opportunity to get it back to a one-score game. However, in the most self-sabotaging way ever, Cousins nearly threw an interception to a defensive lineman; the very next play, Fred Warner peanut-punches the ball out of Bowers hands and the 49ers recover the ball.

Four plays later, the Raiders get a 4th-and-short stop and a turnover on downs for the first time in a long time. Five turnovers were committed by both teams in the third quarter alone.

On the next drive, Cousins hits Michael Mayer for a nice gain and as he fought to reach the goal line, disaster struck. Mayer was tackled and fell on top of a defender, while another 49ers defender punched the ball out of his hands just before he crossed the goal line. Negating a potential score, turning the ball over yet again, giving the 49ers a touchback.

From there, the 49ers would drive past midfield with a few runs. But the lack of a Raiders pass rush gave Purdy enough time to find Jordan Watkins open for a 37-yard touchdown catch.

On the ensuing possession, the Raiders drove to the goal line again, behind a 33-yard catch-and-run from Bowers that appeared to stretch the ball over the pylon but was ruled out of bounds. Cousins' quarterback sneak was stuffed when Warner leaped over the pile after the snap. On the next play, Mayer was called for offensive pass interference, negating his own touchdown catch. Followed up with Cousins' second interception of the game, the second turnover inside the red zone, turnover number four and the third straight turnover.

But the hits just kept on coming; in junk time, Cousins would throw his third interception of the day, fourth straight turnover and fifth total. Cousins had Tre Tucker open deep, loaded up, putting his full body into the throw, only for it to fall short and into the waiting arms of a 49ers defender, mercifully allowing this game to come to an end.

#2677. Nets' Julius Randle doesn't believe team is 'letting go of the rope'

Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle has maintained that the Nets have to work on being more connected as a team when they're facing adversity, especially given that they're 2-8 through their first 10 games. Brooklyn is currently 0-2 on its four-game road trip and while the Nets understand that there are 72 more games to go, Randle is giving his take on where the team stands now.

"Honestly, I'm not really sure. I gotta watch the film, to be honest. But, they were getting a lot of stuff off of switching, and credit to them," Randle said to the media after Sunday's 130-93 loss to the Dallas Mavericks. Brooklyn were within striking distance throughout the first quarter, but the Mavericks built as much as a 26-point lead in the second quarter as the Nets looked discouraged by the growing deficit.

"[We] just got to find a way to get back to being a connected group on both ends. I feel like we do a good job of communicating, but it's not really translating," Randle said when asked for his takeaways from this weekend. "So, [we have to figure out] how to make things translate. Basketball is a funny game; it can turn really quick. So, I think [we have to] continue to be optimistic, stay positive."

This hasn't been the first time that Randle or any of the other players have had to address the team being disconnected and it's easy to see when it comes to the numerous defensive breakdowns. For his part, Randle ended Sunday's loss to the Mavericks with 13 points, four rebounds, and four assists, but he was also a -33 plus/minus, easily the worst mark on the team.

As head coach Jordi Fernandez and center Mo Wagner have spoken on since Sunday's game ended, the Nets eventually have to find a way to get on the same page if they're going to string together some wins. Wednesday's contest pits them against the New Orleans Pelicans (4-7) and if Brooklyn isn't careful, they could find themselves with an 0-3 record on their current road trip.

#2674. Does 49ers trade for Keenan Allen solidify their Super Bowl hopes?

The San Francisco 49ers acquired veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick just hours before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10.

It's no secret around the NFL that the Niners have a shortage of available wideouts, making the addition of Allen all the more vital to San Francisco's passing game.

The 49ers have been dealt injuries throughout the season Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr., De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson and Christian Kirk. Each week, there has been someone in the Niners' WR room who steps up to the mantle. Now, Allen gets his turn as San Francisco found their plug-in at receiver.

He returns to the Bay Area having played his collegiate years at Cal from 2010 to 2012. From Cal, he was selected by San Diego Chargers with the 76th overall pick in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft. Allen was runner-up for Offensive Rookie of the Year but he developed into the Chargers' No. 1-receiver. He would become a six-time Pro Bowl selection in 10 seasons, even as the team moved to Los Angeles.

He spent a season with the Chicago Bears in 2024, then returned to LA for another season with the Chargers. He signed with Indianapolis during the offseason.

With Allen back on the West Coast, the hope is to earn the league's most prized piece of jewelry.

Does Allen have enough left in the tank to help bring a Super Bowl to the Bay Area?

Allen comes to San Francisco as a 34-year-old veteran receiver in his 14th NFL season, which bears the question of if he has enough in the tank to be a contributing piece to the 49ers offense. Allen is added to a star-studded wide receiver room, but still, looming injuries loom are a cause of concern, at least until guys start trending upward.

He'll likely come in as a starter. Allen is known for his elite route-running, high IQ and superb ball-tracking and catching ability. Nothing thrown Allen's way gets dropped.

Allen caught 40 balls for 351 yards and 1 touchdown in eight games with the Colts during the 2026 NFL season. He's shared 22% of targets and has a nearly 69% catch rating. He averages 8.8 yards per catch.

His addition provides Brock Purdy with another weapon to find trust in, especially while the San Francisco receiver room slowly gets healthy. Adding Allen means the team doesn't necessarily have to rush guys back to the field.

Plus, Jordan Watkins is coming off a week where he caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown. He continues to improve. Having a threat like Allen alongside Watkins will likely open things up for himself.

The 49ers are still the favorite to win the Super Bowl with +550 odds, according to BetMGM, currently tied with the Buffalo Bills.

For San Francisco, the team's hopes will ride on health and availability. Allen isn't a young buck anymore at 34. Example A, Evans is 33 years old and look how much time he's missed.

No question at what the 49ers will get from the vets on the field, it's a matter of getting them on the field at 100%. Allen has been relatively healthy in 2026 and that's good news for San Francisco.

Allen appeared in every game, except one, for the Colts having missed Week 4 with a groin injury. Since then, he's been dependable, especially production wise. Maybe not the fantasy pickup he once was, but Allen does the things that contributes to winning football games.

#2672. Hoffenheim claim 2-1 victory over Schalke after early Karius error

Hoffenheim returned to winning ways in the Bundesliga thanks to goals from Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle providing a 2-1 win to see them head into the international break in 9th place. The match was also marked by injury concerns for Schalke, with both goalkeeper Loris Karius and Robin Gosens forced off during the contest.

Hoffenheim made the perfect start when Asllani opened the scoring after just 10 minutes. Schalke goalkeeper Karius was at fault for the goal after attempting to play the ball out from the back, only to see his pass intercepted by the alert Hoffenheim forward, who guided the ball into the net.

The visitors responded positively to falling behind, with Adil Aouchiche going close to an equaliser in the 14th minute. However, Oliver Baumann produced an excellent save to deny the Schalke attacker after Kenan Karaman had created the opportunity.

Schalke's failure to take advantage of their promising start was punished when Hoffenheim doubled their advantage in the 26th minute. Following some patient build-up play, Tim Lemperle exchanged passes with Asllani before calmly slotting the ball past Karius to make it 2-0.

Christian Ilzer's side continued to threaten before the break, with Alexander Prass firing narrowly over after being played through by Lemperle. Robin Gosens also had an opportunity at the other end, but his attempted volley failed to trouble Baumann.

The second half began with a significant setback for Schalke. In the 47th minute, Karius produced an excellent save to deny Asllani, but the goalkeeper subsequently collided with his own defender Gosens as the latter attempted to reach the rebound.

Both players required treatment and were unable to continue. Karius was replaced by Kevin Müller, while Vitalie Becker came on for Gosens in a double injury blow for Miron Muslić's side.

Schalke nevertheless continued to search for a way back into the contest. Soufiane El-Faouzi came particularly close in the 57th minute, striking the crossbar after Baumann had initially saved an effort from Becker.

Hoffenheim thought they had added a third goal shortly afterwards, but Andrej Kramarić was ruled offside. At the other end, Junior Adamu squandered a golden opportunity in the 72nd minute, firing wide from close range after his attempt was deflected by Vladimír Coufal.

Schalke eventually found a breakthrough in the 81st minute. Edin Džeko's header was initially saved by Baumann, but the rebound fell kindly for Adamu, who made no mistake from close range to reduce the deficit to 2-1.

The late goal gave Schalke renewed hope, but Hoffenheim managed to hold on during the closing stages to secure all three points.

The result gives Ilzer's team an important Bundesliga victory, while Schalke are left to reflect on a frustrating evening in Sinsheim. Despite their second-half improvement and late goal, Muslić's side were ultimately unable to recover from their costly first-half mistakes.

#2670. Michigan football donors question Kyle Whittingham's future: Report

There has been turmoil in Ann Arbor this past week, with fans questioning the viability of Kyle Whittingham's tenure -- his press conference sound bites not helping -- and made the worse by Michigan football's loss to Michigan State on Saturday.

After the game, Whittingham staunchly said that he would not make any decisions on offensive coordinator Jason Beck until after the season. However, Beck was summarily fired on Sunday, and Whittingham insisted on Monday that it was his decision after watching game film from Saturday's loss.

However, as On3's Pete Nakos tells it, that sounds a little suspicious compared to what he had been hearing.

Nakos appeared on Crain & Cone on Monday, and he said that no decision on Beck had been made as late as 2 p.m. EST (he was fired near 5 p.m. EST), and it didn't appear that there was any plan to oust Beck by Whittingham at any point.

"I admittedly did check in with some folks around like noon, 1 (p.m.) central yesterday, and the decision had not been made," Nakos said. "And it almost came across that he wasn't planning on making any staffing changes at that point. So Kyle Whittingham comes out this morning, said he made the decision. I did check in, though, midday yesterday before that news came down. There was no plan. So, you know, continue to have conversations, try to find out more about how things conspired."

There have been rumors that the call has come from above Whittingham's head, with athletic director Warde Manuel getting involved, but nothing on the record at this point.

But more than that, Nakos reports that high-level donors and the board of regents are now questioning Whittingham's viability after the loss, given that this team is now 5-4 and hasn't consistently looked up to par.

"The other thing I heard Sunday morning was that I think Saturday night, that loss to Michigan State, as painful as it was for Cone, was also an eye-opener for a lot of donors and some board of trustees to say, 'Oh, like this is where we're at, where we just lost to Michigan State at home,'" Nakos said. "You know, I think playing Indiana tight and trying to find some rhythm against Rutgers, that's kind of like, OK, maybe we're turning the corner, and then you basically go scoreless against one of your archrivals."

Of course, Michigan has a lame duck athletic director in Manuel, who will be stepping down at the end of the year. The Wolverines announced that they have started the search for his replacement, and there are indications that it's escalating.

Nakos says that if Michigan hurriedly gets a new AD, the gears could potentially turn on a decision on Whittingham, one way or the other, sooner than many might think. A new AD doesn't guarantee that the former Utah coach would be out, but it would certainly give the school some clarity.

"Well, I mean, they've started the search, so hypothetically, the new president could make this hire by the end of the month and get the new AD in there immediately," Nakos said. "How that all shakes out, I mean, I know that they're in the early process. But Florida State just hired an athletic director basically in 14 days."

#2669. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni denies giving his fans the middle finger after division loss: 'Absolutely not'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Philadelphia Eagles season isn't exactly going as planned, with a losing record and major injuries. When struggles come in sports, frustrations typically follow and Philly's head coach has been accused of letting out those frustrations with a well-known gesture after their 19-11 divisional loss to the New York Giants on Sunday, the team's first loss in Philadelphia to the Giants since 2013.

Nick Sirianni was called out for what some believe was the head coach giving fans the middle finger as he walked off the field after the Week 9 defeat. In the video, Sirianni looks at his hand, then the middle finger is raised higher than the others as he approaches the tunnel.

Nick Sirianni was asked if he was flipping fans off while walking off the field yesterday. "Absolutely not." #Eagles https://t.co/fqKylEJGxw

— Cory Nidoh (@Cory_Nidoh) November 9, 2026

Sirianni denies any ill will on whatever his hand was doing at the time, saying, "Absolutely not. That was a surprise to me. Absolutely not."

This is not the first time Sirianni and Eagles fans have clashed. In 2024, Sirianni was booed by some fans at Lincoln Financial Field, with some yelling for him to be fired during a game against the then 1-5 Cleveland Browns. Fans weren't happy that the Eagles were struggling, coming off a bye, against an easy opponent. Philadelphia went went on to win the game, though narrowly at 20-16.

As he was walking off the field, Sirianni cupped his ears and yelled at fans. At first, he said he was just "having fun" and was "excited to get the win," but then reversed his messaging, issuing an apology to Eagles fans.

"What I was really doing, I was trying to bring energy yesterday, energy, enthusiasm, and I'm sorry and disappointed on how my energy was directed at the end of the game," he said at the time. "And, you know, my energy should be all in on coaching, motivating and celebrating with our guys. And so I've got to have better wisdom and discernment of when to use that energy and that wasn't the time."

Another notable move from the head coach this Sunday was how long it took to start his press conference, with him taking the podium over an hour after the game ended. He said during that time he was talking to players and didn't reveal exactly what it was about. Typically, press conferences begin much sooner than that for a head coach, so many online pointed out the oddity.

The Eagles currently sit at 2-7 and are on a seven-game losing streak. This marks the worst start during Sirianni's time with the team. This marks the first time since 1999 that the team has started 2-7.

If Sirianni wasn't in the hot seat before (he was), he certainly is now after a bad divisional loss that put them in last in the NFC East.

#2668. Week 10 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Corey Kiner, Tank Dell among top pickups

Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

With Kirk Cousins heading back to Minnesota, the Raiders can finally put their first-overall pick under center. While you're not going to want to use Mendoza against the Seahawks defense this week, his outlook for the rest of the season is quite promising as a highly-drafted pick attached to Klint Kubiak.

The Heisman Trophy winner proved himself to be a good leader in college with excellent on-field awareness and the toughness needed to overcome adversity during games. He has a strong arm to make any throw, but it's his touch passing that stood out. Though Mendoza's not fast enough to be a meaningful runner in the pros, he has enough speed to scramble his way out of trouble and pick up yards on the ground. This all amounts to an intriguing fantasy QB2 with room to grow.

The quarterback position is very picked over at the moment. Malik Willis was featured in this spot last week, but he's now playing through a groin injury that's limited his abilities as a runner and neutered his fantasy potential. So, all that's left are uncomfortable streaming options.

The Steelers are coming off their bye week, which should help the 42-year-old Rodgers (turns 43 in December) feel refreshed for a date with the division rival Bengals.

Rodgers hasn't had many favorable opponents this season, but he did take advantage of his easiest matchup. That just happened to be against the Bengals in Week 3, when the veteran passed for 292 yards and three touchdowns en route to a QB8 finish.

In his last visit to Cincinnati, Rodgers threw four touchdowns back in Week 7 of the 2025 campaign. He's not a slam-dunk streamer, but he's a solid one given the options this week.

Desperation streaming options (if healthy)

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

The elite backup RBs who are one injury away from stardom should be rostered everywhere and I'll continue to highlight them in this space until they no longer qualify for this article.

It was clear early in the season that Johnson was one of the best backups to roster, in case anything ever happens to Kenneth Walker III. In recent weeks, Johnson's value has increased even more now that he's offering weekly flex production.

The rookie posted a fluky 128 receiving yards and a score in Week 8, but he followed it up with 34 yards and another touchdown on Sunday. Upcoming matchups with the Falcons, Cardinals and Bills are all spots where Johnson could be a viable flex play while also offering league-winning upside if Walker ever misses time.

Black is in the same situation as Johnson; you can basically just swap Walker's name with Christian McCaffrey's in the previous section.

The 49ers' rookie plays in one of the best offenses in the league and has flashed his potential with at least 60 rushing yards in three of his first eight games, while serving as CMC's direct backup. That includes the past two games, when Black turned 12 touches into 63 yards and a TD against the Falcons, as well as Sunday's outing, which resulted in 11 carries for a season-high 70 yards.

Next up is the Cowboys defense, which is a top-five matchup for fantasy running backs. The 49ers are 4-point favorites in a game with the highest projected point total in Week 10 at 55.5.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last year is just an obvious move. Black should be rostered everywhere as a flex option with RB1 upside if McCaffrey were ever sidelined.

Rhamondre Stevenson left Sunday's game with a knee injury and was very quickly ruled out. Mike Vrabel didn't have an update Monday morning, but did acknowledge that his back was undergoing an MRI. With TreVeyon Henderson already sidelined indefinitely, that leaves Kiner as the next man up.

Though Kiner hasn't been asked to do much as a pass-catcher, the 2025 UDFA has shown some juice in the run game by topping 50 yards in three of his last five outings in a change-of-pace role.

If Stevenson can't suit up in Week 10, which seems unlikely due to news that he'll probably miss some time, Kiner immediately becomes a high-end fantasy RB3 with the usual touchdown upside that comes with a starter's workload. We can't lock that outcome in, though until we get a proper update on Stevenson's injury.

Josh Jacobs fractured his finger and is set to undergo surgery that will keep him out a maximum of three games.

MarShawn Lloyd missed Week 9 due to a knee injury, which allowed Johnson to step up in Jacobs' absence. Johnson finished with 68 yards and a touchdown, making him the RB11 on the week with just MNF left to be played.

If you're wondering why Johnson isn't higher on this list, just take a look at Green Bay's upcoming schedule. The Packers face the Vikings this week, then have a bye before taking on the Rams.

So, even with Jacobs sidelined, this isn't the ideal setup for a spot starter. On top of that, we aren't sure if/when Lloyd will be available. If Lloyd is active in Week 10, it only further muddies the projections.

If Lloyd remains out, Johnson would be a risky RB3/flex versus the Vikings. If Lloyd plays, then both players would be risky flex options.

With the Saints cutting Kendre Miller, Estimé stepped into a significant role in his first game since joining the Saints. The result was a 47% snap share, which led to 15 carries for 72 yards and a touchdown, as well as another five yards on a catch.

Estimé's presence helped kickstart New Orleans' rushing attack, but his fantasy outlook is directly tied to Travis Etienne Jr.'s health. Etienne, who can be activated off IR at any time, wasn't ready to practice last week. Once we see him back on the field, it will severely diminish Estimé's fantasy value.

However, if Etienne misses another week, fantasy managers will be able to start Estimé as a fringe low-end RB2.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at TEN (33% rostered)

Sione Vaki vs. NE (Germany) (2% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

DeMario Douglas has always been a risky receiver to put in your fantasy lineup due to his low floor. We witnessed that occur in Week 7, when he only delivered three catches for 23 yards.

However, Douglas has posted at least 12 fantasy points in his other four outings over the last five weeks, finishing as a top-10 WR three times. After hauling in five of his nine targets for 102 yards in Week 9, he currently sits as the WR23 with just Monday Night Football remaining.

Four touchdowns during this stretch have helped his cause, but he's come away with very respectable yardage totals in these games with at least 65 in each.

A.J. Brown's recovery timeline remains uncertain and with a bye looming, it seems likely we won't see him until Week 12 at the earliest. Fantasy managers can continue to take advantage by starting Douglas as a WR3/flex option with temporary upside.

Dell's return from a near career-ending injury is one of the best stories in the NFL this season. The fact that he's been productive since getting back on the field only makes it more incredible.

While his 43-yard catch on one target in Week 7 was a bit fluky, it's hard to ignore a nine-target outing this past week. Dell finished the day with four grabs, 105 yards and a score and looked good in the process. However, he still only ran 50% of the routes in a Houston passing attack that's known for rotating receivers behind Nico Collins. We'll need to see more from Dell before we can trust him as an every-week fantasy starter, but he's done enough to warrant being added in most formats as a potential boom-or-bust WR3/flex.

After back-to-back games with at least 50 yards, it was discouraging to see Williams underwhelm with just three catches for 25 yards this week. I'm still holding out hope though.

The rookie continues to play the most snaps and run the most routes in the Commanders' receiver room. This was the third straight outing where Williams accomplished that feat, following Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury.

It's possible Williams levels off as a low-ceiling WR4/flex option for fantasy, but I'm holding for at least another week. The talent is evident and Washington has one of the top-10 easiest schedules for fantasy receivers the rest of the way.

Douglas has played four games this year that weren't impacted by injury. In those contests, the rookie has posted stat lines of 5-94-0, 2-70-2, 4-43-0 and 6-70-0.

With Malik Willis heading to IR, Douglas's fantasy ceiling takes a hit. However, he's still an intriguing rookie who is emerging as the No. 1 target in his offense.

When a first-year player is showing this kind of production early in his career, it's worth taking notice. Even with Kyle McCord under center, Douglas can be started as a WR4/flex given his intriguing matchups against the Colts and Bills the next two weeks.

It's easy to forget, but Bryant had a growing role in the Broncos' passing attack during the opening month before being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In those first four games, Bryant topped 40 yards three times.

So, it was great to see him post a season-high 56 yards and a touchdown on four catches in his first game back since the injury. Jaylen Waddle also suffered a concussion, but he should be cleared after their Week 10 bye.

Regardless, Bryant was a borderline flex option early in the season and has returned with an even better performance. Given Waddle's struggles and Courtland Sutton's age, there's a non-zero chance Bryant becomes the most valuable fantasy receiver in Denver for the rest of the season.

Watkins' fantasy value is difficult to assess because it's entirely dependent on the health of the other receivers in San Francisco.

Keenan Allen was acquired at the trade deadline, but most of the other wideouts on the roster are injured. Deebo Samuel Sr. is nearing a return from a hamstring injury that kept him out for the last month. Mike Evans' Achilles tendinitis is an ongoing problem with no clear recovery timeline. I'll be surprised if he suits up in Week 10. Demarcus Robinson is apparently playing at less than 100%, while De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are on IR.

That opened the door for Watkins, who put up four receptions, 86 yards and a touchdown versus the Raiders. That's his second consecutive quality stat line, after a 56-yard performance versus the Falcons prior to the Niners' Week 8 bye.

If everything remains the same with Evans and Deebo sitting out, Watkins will be a boom-or-bust WR4/flex option in a good matchup with the Cowboys this week. However, once Allen is up to speed and the other receivers are healthy, Watkins won't be worth rostering in redraft leagues.

Jordyn Tyson is 54% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Makai Lemon is 53% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Tyson and D.Douglas, if available.

Courtland Sutton is 53% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Tyson, D. Douglas, Lemon, C. Douglas and Dell, if available.

Khalil Shakir is 53% rostered but would be the No. 9 WR add behind Tyson, D. Douglas, Lemon, C. Douglas, Dell, Williams, Sutton and Bryant, if available.

In the four games since Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has posted stat lines for 4-60-0, 7-69-0, 2-32-0 and 6-57-0.

While he hasn't found the end zone, that type of volume (at least six targets in three of the four appearances) makes him the 10th-most targeted tight end on a per game basis during that stretch.

Okonkwo has moved into the high-end TE2 streamer conversation, with a chance to crack the low-end TE1 range moving forward.

Puka Nacua is heading to IR, Davante Adams is already there and Terrance Ferguson isn't expected back for another couple weeks.

Higbee has disappeared from fantasy relevance following his impressive three-game stretch from Week 3 to Week 5, when he posted 8-62-1, 5-67-0 and 5-83-0. Since then, the veteran has been held to 22 yards or less in four straight contests and hasn't found the end zone.

However, the Rams will have no choice but to increase his targets with Nacua out. That puts Higbee back in the mix as a TE2 streamer with upside.

Eddy Pineiro is 54% rostered but would be the No. 1 K add, if available.

Wide Receivers: Michael Wilson, Xavier Worthy, Chris Godwin Jr., Marvin Harrison Jr., Devaughn Vele

Lamar Jackson is undergoing surgery that will sideline him for 6-10 weeks. If you're stashing him in hopes that he'll return for the fantasy playoffs, you're wasting a roster spot.

Despite the Texans making a trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., he's just part of a big rotation of receivers behind Nico Collins. It's possible MHJ could carve out a bigger role as the season progresses, but it's highly unlikely he'll make a major fantasy impact — unless Collins gets hurt. Even in that scenario, I'm not confident Harrison would step up.

With Jordyn Tyson now in the lineup, Devaughn Vele's days as a fantasy flex option are over.

The AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) are loading up for a run at the Super Bowl just ahead of the trade deadline. After trading for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux, they are trading for another defender Monday afternoon: Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis.

The Jaguars are sending the Eagles a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Davis, the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia who was a starter on the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX title team in the 2024 season. This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2664. Why NFL trade deadline evolved from afterthought to hectic: In-season transaction boom is league's new normal

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Less than a decade ago, it was common for the NFL to feature single-digit trades during the course of the regular season. The trade deadline was generally a snoozer in comparison to that of the other major American professional sports leagues, and the number of moves made at the buzzer could often be counted on one hand. That could not be further from the case anymore.

Twenty-four hours out from the 2026 trade deadline, there were 10 in-season trades in the books. That number will balloon in the final hours before the clock strikes 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10. Star players could be on the move as Super Bowl contenders gear up for the stretch run and teams falling out of contention seek to jumpstart their rebuilds with premium draft capital. Basketball and baseball fans are used to seeing this flurry of transactions, but it is still relatively new to football fans. Just like in the other leagues, though, this boom is becoming the NFL's new normal.

Last year, there were 22 trades from the first day of the regular season through the deadline. That was the most in any year since at least 1995, according to NFL Research. A whopping 12 players and 14 picks were exchanged on deadline day alone. General managers were busier than ever. That was the extreme continuation of a trend that has been in effect since the mid-2010s, in which front offices mortgage their futures for instant-impact players or, conversely, sell off their most valuable assets to hoard draft picks.

Only once from 2010 through 2017 did the NFL log 12 or more in-season trades, according to the Spotrac trade tracker. Something flipped towards the end of the decade, because that number now represents the low-water mark since 2018.

Why the sudden uptick? There are fundamental processes in the NFL that make this league more trade-averse than other sports leagues, but changes to the calendar and new front-office philosophies have created pathways for teams to bypass some of the roadblocks.

Trading players in the NFL is not as simple as matching salaries. That is largely why player-for-player trades remain so rare. The way contracts are structured, with teams spreading bonuses out across multiple years, taking on dead money and being on the hook for some of the salary owed to the players they trade away, is sometimes prohibitive. Plus, the NFL has a hard salary cap, so unlike in the NBA, where teams use exceptions to go over the cap, or in MLB, where wealthy owners can pony up as much money as they please, all deals have to result in both teams remaining under that firm number.

Football is also not as plug-and-play as other sports. There are massive playbooks to learn, especially at the offensive skill positions. There is incredibly important timing to perfect, particularly for the quarterback-wide receiver tandem. With 11 players on the field at all times and complicated schemes to comprehend, anyone who joins a lineup in the middle of the season has a lot of learning to do on the fly.

The brevity of a 17-game regular season also keeps a larger percentage of the league in playoff contention deeper into the year compared to 82- or 162-game campaigns. The lack of non-contenders means fewer teams are willing to sell, and thus there is a smaller volume of available players.

Draft picks are also immensely valuable since teams have so many roster spots to fill. And at the same time, rosters are so large that fringe players around the 53-man cutoff can simply be released if the potential trade package is undesirable.

Until 2011, the NFL trade deadline was extremely early in the season. It landed on the Tuesday following Week 6, which was well before the midway point of the campaign. Teams were often still attempting to figure out where they stood in the pecking order when it came time to lock in their rosters. How could a general manager shop one of his stars on an expiring contract when they were not sure whether their team was in the mix for a postseason berth or not? They rarely did.

That changed in 2012 when the NFL and NFL Players Association agreed to move the deadline back by two weeks to the Tuesday following Week 8. And not long after the league adopted a 17th regular-season game, it moved the deadline back another week to where it stands now: The Tuesday after Week 9, which is effectively the midseason point.

It is far clearer where teams stand in the playoff picture after Week 9 than after Week 6. Look no further than the Indianapolis Colts, who emerged as one of the NFL's most aggressive sellers this year. Through six games, they were 2-4 and competitive enough in a couple of their losses to believe that they could right the ship. Now, after nine games, they are a measly 2-7 and own a five-game losing streak. Clearly out of the postseason hunt, they moved on from perennial Pro Bowlers in Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.

Perhaps the single most impactful change in the rise of in-season trades comes from the mentality surrounding draft picks. While the value of Day 1 picks in the NFL is still tremendous, it is more common now than ever to see general managers move that sacred capital for players who can help them win at the highest level right away instead of a couple of years down the line. Nowhere is this clearer than in Los Angeles, where Rams general manager Les Snead birthed the "F them picks" mantra.

Each of those moves opened or extended the Rams' championship contention windows. They are bets on current stars and their ability to keep playing at a high level, compared to the risk of boom-or-bust picks in the late first round. In order to balance the roster, Snead relies on finding diamonds in the rough in the later rounds, which he has been highly successful at pulling off.

This model delivered a Super Bowl and proved to other teams that it is a viable strategy for roster construction. In the copycat league that is the NFL, the Rams are no longer the only team to go all in to fuel championship runs.

Snead even has direct disciples putting his methodology to practice in other places. Jacksonville Jaguars general manager James Gladstone worked under Snead's tutelage in various roles for nine years before he landed a GM job of his own. On Monday, he pulled off two trades in which he swapped draft picks for immediate-impact players. They may not have been Day 1 picks, but they were draft capital nonetheless.

Draft picks are still gold, even in this era where they are moved like never before. General managers who want the best of both worlds -- to hoard picks and secure immediate impacts -- can balance the two, but they have to be creative. Enter the pick swap. Instead of one team netting a draft pick while the other loses one, pick swaps allow teams to generate value in the aggregate while retaining at least some capital. If a player is valued around a late-Day 2 pick, the buying team could send a second-rounder and receive a Day 3 pick in return along with that player.

Compensatory picks also give general managers the flexibility to take swings at available players. If there is a veteran on an expiring contract who can join a team as a half-season rental, the buying franchise may give up a third-round pick or worse to acquire them, knowing that they can recoup the pick if the player leaves in free agency.

Gladstone himself pulled off a masterful move ahead of Tuesday's deadline by factoring compensatory picks into the equation. He reached a deal with the New Orleans Saints that sent Davon Godchaux to Jacksonville in exchange for a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick. That pick would become a 2027 sixth-rounder if the Jaguars acquire one through another trade or through the compensatory formula. In essence, Gladstone traded a pick he does not even own yet.

So many things in football are cyclical, but the surge in trade deadline action has staying power. Changes at the league level with regard to scheduling have made it more viable, and general managers are as aggressive as ever in a "what have you done for me lately" world. Now that front offices have another tool at their disposal in roster construction, it will only become more mainstream. The cat is out of the bag, and it will be hard to put it back in.

#2663. 2026 NFL Trade Deadline Fantasy Fallout: Josh Downs gets massive QB upgrade with move to Chiefs

The NFL Trade Deadline is complete and fantasy football is in a whirlwind! Fantasy analyst Joel Smyth breaks down some key deals — first up, the Colts' trade of Josh Downs to Kansas City.

This trade is not only a win but life-saving for Josh Downs' fantasy outlook (you can read the full trade terms here). The dynasty fantasy winner of the day, and he can finally be usable in redraft leagues!

The Colts had injuries to Alec Pierce, traded away Michael Pittman Jr. and Downs was still limited to a sub-20% target share. Kansas City has a similar lack of pass catchers as Indianapolis, but gives Downs more of a chance as one of the most talented receivers in a new offense. He should fit well on a team that has the lowest average depth of target in the NFL.

I'm worried for Rashee Rice once Downs is playing full snaps. Rice is a volume-dependent WR who has recently been looking much improved compared to the first few weeks of the season. However, his style is very similar to Downs, running over 50% of routes from the slot and having over 70% of receiving fantasy points coming on throws under 10 air yards. The big positive here is the schedule — not in terms of fantasy points allowed to WRs, but the game scripts ahead. In a five-game stretch, the Chiefs play the Bills, Rams, Bengals, Patriots and 49ers, all teams that can bump up the passing volume and scoring.

That schedule might be more impactful for Mahomes than Josh Downs, although it is a positive. The passing production for Mahomes over the past few years has been modest in fantasy, often relying on his rushing for his ceiling, and I'm not sure this massively changes anything. It's a plus, but maybe a 1-PPG bump compared to having a different wideout in the ball game.

#2661. NFL news, live updates, trade deadline rumors: Vikings trade for QB Kirk Cousins; Colts don't trade Jonathan Taylor, send Josh Downs to Chiefs

Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, and we've got the NFL trade deadline on deck, which is set for Tuesday afternoon at 4 p.m. ET. Buckle up!

The biggest news of the day — the Minnesota Vikings have traded for Kirk Cousins in a reported deal with the Las Vegas Raiders, sending a third-round pick to Vegas in exchange for the vet. The move reunites Cousins with the Vikings, for whom he last played in 2023 before suffering a torn Achilles, and gives Minnesota some much-needed support at quarterback following Monday night's abysmal loss under Carson Wentz.

The Jacksonville Jaguars kicked off the NFL trade news cycle for the week with a splash move to bolster the secondary, sending a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons in exchange for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III. They continued adding on defense throughout the day, also acquiring Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints and former first-round pick Jordan Davis in a blockbuster deal with the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Indianapolis Colts were another team to watch ahead of the trade deadline, with star running back Jonathan Taylor at the crux of it all. But as was first reported by NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Colts did not trade Taylor ahead of Tuesday's deadline. The Colts did, however, trade wide receiver Josh Downs, who gets a fresh start with the Kansas City Chiefs and quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 9.

After a great deal of speculation was made that Jonathan Taylor could be moved ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly standing pat.

The team will not trade him ahead of the deadline, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Tuesday afternoon.

Pelissero reported that the Colts had received multiple offers for Taylor of a second-round pick-plus, but instead, the team will move forward with him as a foundational piece within the locker room as they look to rebuild.

The Dallas Cowboys have signed former Saints running back Kendre Miller to their practice squad, according to multiple reports.

Miller played sparingly in three-plus seasons as a backup for the Saints, tallying 656 rushing yards on 3.6 yards per carry in 27 appearances. The Saints released the former third-round pick on Saturday after signing Audric Estime off waivers from the Cleveland Browns.

With backup running back Tyler Goodson sidelined with a knee sprain, Miller adds a potential depth piece behind starter Javonte Williams.

Acquiring Kirk Cousins wasn't the only notable Vikings roster move on Tuesday.

Shortly after Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, the Vikings announced that they have released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. Per NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Beckham will re-sign with Minnesota's practice squad.

The transaction clears a spot on the 53-man roster that can make room for Cousins.

Beckham joined the Vikings after being released by the Giants three games into his return to New York. Beckham played in just one game for Minneosta, Monday's disastrous loss to the Bills that ultimately prompted them to trade for Cousins on Tuesday. He did not catch a pass for the Vikings.

The Ravens and Falcons pulled off a buzzer-beater trade right at the deadline.

Baltimore sent G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 6th-round pick to Atlanta for C Ryan Neuzil, per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones.

Vorhees was a backup guard for the Ravens, while Neuzil was the Falcons' starting center.

The Miami Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve on Tuesday, the team announced.

Willis has had a lingering groin injury that has been impacting his mobility. The quarterback had an MRI, and it showed that it is now a core muscle injury. Willis doesn't need surgery, but the amount of rest required to recover made it make sense for Miami to add him to IR.

With Willis sidelined for at least the next month, backup quarterback Kyle McCord is expected to take over as the starter this weekend against the Indianapolis Colts, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Willis is not expected to miss the remainder of the season.

The Tennessee Titans reportedly received interest in running back Tony Pollard at the trade deadline, but will keep the veteran around, according to ESPN.

With just minutes left before the deadline, it looks like it will be a weak deadline for running backs. Pollard isn't the only significant name staying put, as the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly holding on to Jonathan Taylor as well.

The Kansas City Chiefs have reportedly traded for wide receiver Josh Downs in a deal with the Indianapolis Colts, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported.

Per NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Chiefs sent 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks to the Colts in exchange for Downs and a 2027 seventh-rounder.

The Chiefs were reportedly in the market for a wide receiver for quarterback Patrick Mahomes, particularly after Xavier Worthy suffered a hamstring in Week 9. Now, they get a high-upside option in Downs, whose rookie contract will expire at the end of this season.

Downs amassed 2,494 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns over four seasons with the Colts, but his tenure there has largely been marked by turnover at the quarterback position.

In his career, he's caught passes from current QB Daniel Jones, Gardner Minshew II, Joe Flacco, Anthony Richardson Sr., Philip Rivers and Riley Leonard. Mahomes is no doubt an upgrade as Downs looks to prove himself in a contract year.

The Chargers are trading linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. L.A. gets back a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.

Henley, 26, leads the Chargers with 51 tackles. He also has 2.5 tackles for loss, including 0.5 sacks. The linebacker has one interception, a forced fumble, and two fumble recoveries.

Henley is in the final year of his rookie deal.

With their sights set on a Super Bowl title, the Buffalo Bills are adding a dynamic defensive playmaker in trading for Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reports.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Bills are sending the Titans a second-round draft pick and will also receive a fifth-round selection in return.

The move bolsters a defense that ranks 29th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game. Hooker joins the Bills tied for the league lead with five interceptions alongside six passes defended.

The Bills made the move after reportedly inquiring about eight-time Pro Bowl Cardinals safety Budda Baker.

After watching Carson Wentz crash and burn during a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9, the Minnesota Vikings came into Tuesday with one extremely obvious goal: Get another quarterback.

The team followed through on that promise, acquiring Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero.

The Raiders will reportedly receive a 2027 third-round pick in exchange for the veteran quarterback.

The Raiders also inquired about Justin Herbert, Daniel Jones and Geno Smith, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports.

Cousins was the most obvious fit. Once it became clear the Vikings would be in the market for a quarterback at the trade deadline, both Cousins and Indianapolis Colts starter Daniel Jones came up as popular options, as both players spent time with the team in recent seasons.

Of that pair, Cousins has actually performed well this season. Thanks to his resurgence, the Raiders rank a surprising eighth in points per game in 2026. The team ranked dead last in that category last season.

Cousins has played a significant role in the team's offensive turnaround. The 38-year-old has thrown 20 touchdowns against eight interceptions in nine games. Only Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has more passing touchdowns this season, and he's getting MVP buzz.

Keenan Allen is reportedly headed back to California, this time to play for the San Francisco 49ers.

Allen, best known for his time with the Chargers, is being traded midway through his first season with the Indianapolis Colts, according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix, who reported ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline that the Colts are receiving a 2027 sixth-round pick from the Niners in exchange.

Could Las Vegas Raiders QB Kirk Cousins actually be headed back to Minnesota to play for a quarterback-needy Vikings team?

Well, it sounds like the Vikings are seriously interested. The team has identified the 38-year-old Cousins — who spent 2018-23 in Minnesota — as a "prime trade candidate" ahead of today's trade deadline, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Of course, the Raiders would have to be willing to part with the veteran. He's been their bridge signal-caller this season, posting a 20:8 touchdown-to-interception ratio while mentoring this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza.

Your eyes didn't deceive you after that MNF QB performance for Minnesota.

The 27-year-old Ebiketie was in his first season with the Eagles after signing a one-year deal in free agency in March. Before coming to Philadelphia, he spent he spent four seasons with the Falcons after being a second-round draft pick by Atlanta in 2022.

In nine games this season, Ebiketie has 23 total tackles and three for loss.

We'll see if the Jaguars are done dealing after acquiring Jordan Davis, Davon Godchaux and Jessie Bates III on Monday, but one player reportedly staying put is wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

#2657. Tiger Woods 'feeling better' after car crash and arrest before Hero World Challenge, unclear if he will play in Bahamas

Tiger Woods will be on the golf course in the Bahamas next month regardless. Whether he tees it up at the Hero World Challenge, though, is still a mystery.

Woods, who hasn't played competitive golf since the TGL Final days before his crash and arrest in Florida, told Sirius XM PGA Tour Radio on Tuesday that he's "feeling better" and has been "training quite a bit."

While nothing is official and he's not announced any plans, that's undoubtedly a good sign for the 50-year-old with the new PGA Tour season just a few months out.

"I'm feeling better, there's no doubt about that," Woods said. "I've been training quite a bit."

"I will be at Hero," he added with a laugh. "I'm there either way, so I'll see you there."

Woods has hosted the Hero World Challenge, an unofficial Tour event, for years now in the Bahamas. The no-cut tournament has just a 20-man field, and still has three spots open. If Woods wants to play again, that'd be a very easy spot to return.

Woods appeared in a TGL match last season in March, but he was involved in a rollover crash just days later in Jupiter Island, Florida. He was preparing to return for the Masters the next month, but ended up pleading guilty to misdemeanor charges of reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test after his arrest. His driver's license was suspended for five years as a result, too.

Woods hasn't played anywhere since, and has only made a handful of public appearances. He stepped away from the sport and reportedly sought treatment in Switzerland, too.

It's unclear when Woods will play again. He is reportedly expected to compete in the new TGL season in December, though indoor golf is very different from the real thing, especially from a physical standpoint.

Woods ruptured his Achilles and underwent back surgery in 2025, and missed all four major championships that season as a result. The 50-year-old has only played a full tournament in three of his last 11 starts, and has otherwise missed the cut or withdrawn. He last played on the PGA Tour at the British Open in 2024.

There are a few other options for Woods to make his Tour return, if it's not at the Hero World Challenge. He could play alongside his son, Charlie, at the PNC Championship — a 36-hole parent-child event that would allow him to use a cart. He could wait until the Genesis Invitational next season in Los Angeles, too. Woods hosts that event on the Tour each season, and it would be an easy starting point before the major championships get going.

Regardless of what he ends up doing, Woods appears to be in a much better spot now than he was just a few months ago. A return to the sport appears imminent.

#2654. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B
